statement: Let G=(V,E) be a finite tree. Then |E| = |V| - 1.
proof: We argue by induction on |V|. If |V|=1, then G has no edges. Otherwise, choose a leaf v, let G' = G - v, and apply the induction hypothesis to G'. Since v is a leaf, deleting v removes one vertex and one edge. Hence |E|-1 = (|V|-1)-1, so |E| = |V|-1.
local_context: Classical finite graph theory theorem used as the first reference example.
